text:
Leonard V: Quick sync - we need a low-friction plan to move users off org-global API keys to minimum-scope keys. customer infra hit a blast radius last week when a leaked key touched billing APIs.
Priya S: ouch. Do we have telemetry on how many tokens are global vs project-scoped?
Tom R: roughly 72% global, 20% project, 8% service-specific according to last export. most webhooks and infra scripts use global keys.
Olga M: big migration surface. customers won't like forced rollouts. we should do opt-in first and then auto-migrate with a safe fallback.
Leonard V: high-level goals: 1) Reduce blast radius (min-scope by default) 2) Minimal customer friction 3) Preserve existing integration patterns for internal automation.
Priya S: constraint: third-party integrations that only support a single key per org. can't break them.
Tom R: idea: create a compatibility layer where a global key can mint time-limited project-scoped tokens on first use. keep audit trail linking minted token to original key.
Olga M: that's smart. runtime token minting avoids immediate breaking. but need rate limits + throttles for mint endpoint.
Leonard V: tradeoffs: - Pros: seamless for customers, gradual reduction in real privileges - Cons: complexity in authn path, potential token sprawl, extra latency on cold mint.
Priya S: ops questions: where to store mapping? do we keep original key as canonical owner and minted tokens ephemeral? TTL suggestion: minted tokens default 24h, extendable policies.
Tom R: implement as: global_key -> KMS-wrapped minting secret -> issue JWT scoped to project. JWT contains parent_key_id and minted_by claim. sample payload: {"iss":"authn.redwood","sub":"token-abc","scope":"project:123:write","parent_key":"k_org_789"} .
Olga M: need to update audit UI to show parent_key in the event view and let SecOps filter on parent key.
Leonard V: enforcement model: 1) phase 1 (60 days): compatibility minting enabled for orgs, guidance doc + SDK updates 2) phase 2 (60-120 days): send deprecation warnings when global key used for project APIs 3) phase 3: optional hard-block in dedicated mode (enterprise customers can opt-out).
Priya S: compliance: rotation rules must apply to parent keys. revoking parent key should invalidate minted tokens immediately. how to revoke? track parent_key_id in token so introspection can reject if revoked.
Tom R: introspection endpoint checks parent_key_state in authn DB. add signal to push revocation to token-cache and edge. TTL for minted tokens should be short to keep window small.
Olga M: test matrix: - web UI sign-in flows - CLI auth for long-running jobs - webhook consumers - marketplace integrations. Also perf test for mint endpoint QPS under cold cache.
Leonard V: metrics to track: percent global usage, minted-token creation rate, average mint latency, number of revocations, SLO errors caused by minting.
Priya S: security review: need threat model doc: attacker with leaked global key can still mint scoped tokens until parent revoked. accept risk but document mitigations (IP restrictions, 2fa, rotation).
Tom R: rollout tasks: A) SDK support for auto-mint B) mint service + KMS changes C) audit UI change D) CLI update E) docs + customer comms. estimate 6-8 sprints if scoped.
Olga M: can we parallelize? DevEx do SDK/CLI + docs, AuthN do mint service, Console do audit UI. security does threat model and review.
Leonard V: assigning: Priya owns threat model + comms, Tom owns mint service prototype, Olga owns test plan + Console changes, I'll coordinate and draft the phased rollout calendar.
sec-bot: Reminder: open a security review ticket (SEC-2026) and add sec-review label to PRs. Include threat-model artifact.
Priya S: I'll open SEC-2026 and start the threat checklist today.
Leonard V: OK team, thanks. I'll post a short RFC with the prototype link and timeline by EOD. :rocket:
